biography: Marcelo Franco, born in the heart of São Paulo, Brazil, carries the passion of his homeland in every fiber of his being. Growing up near Interlagos, the roar of engines was his lullaby. His father, a mechanic for a local karting team, introduced him to the world of motorsport. Marcelo's talent became evident early, dominating the Brazilian karting scene. At age 16, during a regional karting event, his kart spun out, narrowly avoiding a serious collision – a moment that instilled in him a blend of caution and aggression. He transitioned to Formula Renault, then to Formula 3 Sudamericana, securing several wins before finally landing a seat with MitSport. Though flashes of brilliance mark his career, inconsistency has been his Achilles heel, a constant battle against his own fluctuating temperament. Now at 32, he finds himself at what should be his peak, fighting to harness his raw talent into consistent performance.
drivingStyle: Franco's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach. He's known for his aggressive overtakes and late braking maneuvers, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. Tire management is a known weakness; he tends to overdrive early in stints, sacrificing long-run pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, Franco can either elevate his performance to another level or succumb to costly errors, a testament to his inconsistent nature. His qualifying is generally strong, allowing him to start near the front, where his aggressive style can pay dividends, or lead to early incidents.

rivalries.reason: Rossi, a calculated and consistent driver, represents everything Franco isn't. Their contrasting styles often clash on track, leading to heated battles and occasional accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.
Tanaka and Franco were teammates in Formula 3. Despite being friends off the track, their competitive natures led to several on-track incidents and a constant battle for team leadership.
Silva, a veteran driver, often criticizes Franco's aggressive style, labeling him reckless and dangerous. Franco, in turn, dismisses Silva as being past his prime and too cautious.

quirks: Always wears the same faded Senna t-shirt under his race suit.
Listens to a specific samba track right before getting into the car.
Sharpens his racing gloves' seams with a small knife before every session.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix in 2028, a home victory that sent the crowd into a frenzy and solidified his place as a national hero.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the last lap of the Monaco Grand Prix in 2029, costing him a potential victory and severely damaging his championship hopes.
